title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbooks
author: Priya Nair
summary: Canonical SRE guidance for defining SLOs and error budgets, running burn-rate based paging, capacity planning cadence, incident review standards, and operational runbooks for Redwood Inference production services.
body:
Overview
========
This document describes Redwood Inference SRE standards for service-level objectives (SLOs), error budget policies and burn-rate escalation, capacity planning and forecasting, incident review expectations, and operational runbooks. It is intended for on-call engineers, service owners, product managers, and platform teams.

Audience and scope
- Primary: on-call SREs, service owners, platform engineers.
- Scope: all externally visible customer-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated pools, and private control plane).

Guiding principles
- User-facing latency and correctness are first-class SLOs.
- SLOs must be measurable with a single, well-defined signal and a clear window.
- Error budgets enable product velocity; exhaustion triggers measured mitigations.
- Capacity planning is tied to SLOs and business commitments (SLA-backed Dedicated customers).

SLOs and Error Budgets
======================
Minimum metadata required for every SLO:
1. service_name (string)
2. slo_signal (what we measure; e.g., p95 request latency, availability by HTTP 200 success, embedding correctness)
3. objective (percentage over a rolling window)
4. measurement_window (e.g., 30d rolling, 7d rolling)
5. owner (team and primary on-call)
6. alerting thresholds and burn-rate policy

Reference SLO table (examples)
| service | signal | objective | window | owner | notes |
|---------|--------|-----------:|--------|-------|------|
| hosted-api-text-gen | availability (HTTP 2xx) | 99.9% | 30d rolling | eng-serving-runtime | SLA-targeted for paid tier |
| hosted-api-text-gen | latency (p95 total gen time) | < 300ms | 7d rolling | eng-serving-runtime | measured client-side and edge |
| embeddings-service | availability | 99.95% | 30d rolling | eng-platform | high-volume batch and sync use cases |
| dedicated-gpu-pool | throughput (tokens/sec per pool) | capacity target as contract | monthly window | eng-sre | Contract-specific SLOs |

Measurement and instrumentation
- Primary metrics: Prometheus counters/gauges for request counts, errors, latency histograms (client and server-side where applicable).
- Golden events: define what constitutes an error (5xx, model crash, data-exhaustion).
- Tagging: metrics must include service, region, model_id, route, and customer_tier labels.
- Aggregation: use 5m scrape resolution, 1m cardinality rollups for SLO eval.
- Backfilling/mitigation: any retroactive metric correction must be documented and routed through SRE review.

Alerting and burn-rate policy
- Primary on-call alert: when 1-hr burn rate > 2x expected (for a 30d SLO) OR exhaustion predicted within 24 hours.
- Severity escalation levels (automated via Alertmanager / PagerDuty):
  1) Warning: burn rate > 1.2x expected for 1h — notify service owner and SRE via #sre-warnings.
  2) Action: burn rate > 2x for 15m OR remaining error budget < 25% — page primary SRE.
  3) Critical: remaining error budget < 5% OR predicted exhaustion in < 2h — page SRE leads and engage product.
- Default burn-rate multipliers: 1h window uses 24x multiplier relative to 30d budget. Adjust per-service as needed.

Error budget governance
- If a service exhausts >50% of monthly error budget within the first 7 days: immediate triage, retrospective, and temporary deployment freeze for non-essential changes.
- Exhaustion outcomes: rollback of risky rollouts, increase in capacity allocation, or rollout of conservative model variant.
- Reporting: weekly error-budget dashboard emailed to service owners and product managers.

Capacity planning
=================
Cadence and roles
- Quarterly capacity review (eng-sre + eng-platform + product) for major forecasts and contract reviews.
- Monthly operational capacity check for pool utilization, tail latency, and hot-shard indicators.
- Owner: eng-sre capacity squad (primary contact in ownership table below).

Inputs and model
- Inputs: historical QPS, tokens-per-request trends, growth rate, planned feature releases, committed Dedicated capacity, and regional traffic split.
- Safety margin: target 20% spare steady-state capacity and 40% burst headroom for peak 99th percentile traffic unless contract dictates otherwise.
- Planning spreadsheet columns (required): month, baseline_qps, growth_pct, expected_tokens_per_q, provisioned_gpus, expected_utilization_pct, spare_capacity_pct, risk_notes.

Forecast example (single-row CSV style)
- month: 2026-05, baseline_qps: 12k, growth_pct: 8, tokens_per_q: 120, provisioned_gpus: 80 A100-80GB equiv, expected_utilization_pct: 65, spare_capacity_pct: 25, risk_notes: planned marketing push May 10.

Scaling policies and autoscaling runbook
1. Vertical: adjust instance size/shape and model quantization profile for short-term needs.
2. Horizontal: add dedicated GPU nodes, respecting placement (region/az) and data residency.
3. Burst policy: short-lived burst pools (up to +30% capacity) for 2–6 hours per incident window.
4. Pre-warm procedure: 1) schedule pre-warm 30m before expected spike; 2) run synthetic load test 10m prior; 3) verify KV cache hitrates and model loading logs.

Operational Runbooks (standard format)
- Each runbook must include: scope, owner, severity mapping, trigger conditions, immediate mitigation steps, diagnostic commands, rollback steps, follow-up/RCA checklist, and postmortem owner.

Runbook: High Error Rate (5xx spike)
Scope: API routes returning elevated 5xx rates affecting customer requests.
Trigger:
- 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR p50 error rate increase > 5x normal.
Immediate steps:
1. Acknowledge pager and set incident context in Incident Channel (#incident-<service>-yyyyMMdd).
2. Check Grafana dashboard: error rate, request rate, latency, and model process memory.
3. Run diagnostics:
   - kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=<service> -o wide
   - kubectl logs -n prod <pod> --tail=200 | grep -i error
   - curl -sS "https://internal-metrics/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total{code=~\"5..\"}[5m])"
4. If CPU/memory OOM or model OOM: scale down batch sizes or restart affected pods with graceful drain.
5. If model failure: switch traffic to fallback model variant (see rollout policies), update route in the traffic router, and monitor.
6. If external dependency: engage dependency owner and enable degraded-mode fallback.
Post-incident
- Run the incident review within 72 hours. Fill the incident postmortem template and link to the runbook.

Runbook: Latency Tail Spike (p99 increases)
Trigger:
- p99 latency > SLO threshold for 15m or p95 > safety threshold for 30m.
Immediate steps:
1. Validate whether spike is client- or server-side: compare edge p99 vs backend p99.
2. Inspect model serving metrics: KV cache hitrate, batch sizes, GPU utilization, kernel time.
3. Temporarily reduce batch size for latency-sensitive routes (feature flag).
4. If due to cache churn, enable prefix caching for heavy customers and rollback recent cache invalidations.

Incident review standards
========================
- Timeline: initial incident doc within 24h, full postmortem within 72h.
- Required sections: summary, impact, timeline, root cause analysis, corrective actions, monitoring/alerting changes, ownership for actions, and follow-up deadlines.
- Severity classification: Sev-1 (customer impact > 1h or degraded SLA), Sev-2 (partial degradation), Sev-3 (minor/operational).
- RCA expectations: identify broken hypothesis, show evidence (metrics/logs), and list reproducible steps or synthetic tests.
- Action items: must include owner, due date, and verification test. Unverified items escalate to SRE manager after 14 days.

Operational tooling and dashboards
- Observability stack: Prometheus (metrics), Cortex/Thanos (long-term), Grafana (dashboards), Loki (logs), Jaeger (traces), BigQuery (ad-hoc analysis).
- Alerts: managed in Alertmanager with route labels mapping to PagerDuty escalation policies.
- SLO dashboards: per-service SLO panel with burn-rate, error budget remaining (30d), and burn-rate forecast (1h/6h/24h).
- Runbook links: every major dashboard must contain a prominent link to the primary runbook.

Reliability initiatives (examples and playbooks)
- Initiative: Reduce tail latency for hosted-api-text-gen\  - Goal: decrease p99 from 950ms -> 400ms within Q2; reduce variance by 50%\  - Approach: KV cache improvements, kernel tuning, adaptive batching, and tail-sampling traces.
- Initiative: Improve embedding throughput cost by 30%\  - Goal: lower tokens-per-embedding cost via quantized models and request-level caching.
- Initiative: Resilience for Dedicated customers\  - Goal: ensure warm standby pools and automated failover with <60s RTO for critical contracts.

Ownership and contacts
- eng-sre on-call rotation: primary@sre.redwood.ai (PagerDuty)\- eng-platform capacity: capacity-leads@redwood.ai
- product escalation: product-ops@redwood.ai

Change control and rollout guidance
- Canary windows: default 5% traffic for 2h, observe SLOs, then 25% for 4h before full rollout.
- Rollback criteria: SLO degradation > 0.1% absolute or error budget burn > 25% during rollout window.

Reporting and audits
- Weekly SLO health email (automated) to execs and product owners.
- Quarterly reliability review: present open action items, major incidents, and trend charts.
- SLA audit: before renewal of Dedicated contracts, run an SLO evidence pack (30d metrics, deploy history, incident logs).

Appendix: Useful commands and queries
- SLO remaining (PromQL): 1 - sum(increase(http_requests_errors_total[30d])) / sum(increase(http_requests_total[30d]))
- Burn-rate forecast (example): use the SLO microservice to compute projected exhaustion: /api/v1/slo/forecast?service=<service>&window=30d
- Example k8s debug: kubectl -n prod exec -it <pod> -- /bin/bash && ps aux | grep model

Related pages and references
- Logging and observability standards: /confluence/eng-sre/observability-standards
- Incident process: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Model serving standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/model-serving-standards

Document maintenance
- Owner: eng-sre (capacity squad)
- Review cadence: annual review or after each Sev-1 incident.
- Contact the SRE doc maintainer for edits or suggestions.
notes: This document consolidates existing runbooks, SLO definitions, and policies into a single canonical reference. Replace service-specific thresholds with values from individual service SLO pages where necessary.
